query: FCC high-entropy alloys lose substantial strength above 800 °C, motivating refractory high-entropy alloys. Equal-atomic, single-phase BCC NbMoTaW retains excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but has poor room-temperature ductility, and its irradiation resistance has been inferred computationally rather than established here experimentally. Studies of other refractory high-entropy alloys have found greater irradiation resistance than pure tungsten under helium implantation and self-healing behavior associated with enhanced atomic diffusion and redistribution. However, irradiation-induced amorphization, helium-energy-dependent blistering, and irradiation-enhanced precipitation have also been observed, indicating unresolved phase- and surface-stability risks. Given the need to preserve BCC structural stability and high-temperature mechanical performance while improving room-temperature ductility and irradiation tolerance, what intervention could achieve this balance? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted directional or quantitative outcomes relative to untreated NbMoTaW, the applicable temperature and irradiation boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding Re to equiatomic NbMoTaW (forming NbMoTaWRe) improves room-temperature ductility and irradiation tolerance by refining grains, increasing lattice distortion, and forming amorphous intergranular regions that act as defect sinks, thereby suppressing He bubble growth and grain-boundary segregation.
generation.material_initial_state: As-deposited, single-BCC-phase, columnar nanocrystalline Nb25Mo25Ta25W25 films and Nb20Mo20Ta20W20Re20 films magnetron-sputtered onto Si(111).
generation.intervention: Incorporation of Re (approximately 20 at%) into the equiatomic NbMoTaW alloy to form NbMoTaWRe.
generation.conditions: Films are processed at room temperature; irradiation is performed with 120 keV He2+ ions at a fluence of 1×10^16 ions/cm^2 and a dose rate of 1×10^13 ions/cm^2/s for 1000 s; tests are conducted under these irradiation conditions and within the ~400 nm irradiated depth.
generation.structural_mediator: Re addition leads to grain refinement, increased lattice distortion with excess free volume, and the formation of several-nanometer-wide amorphous regions at grain boundaries which serve as effective defect-sink sites.
generation.mechanism: The enhanced defect-sink capacity accelerates the annihilation of irradiation-induced vacancies, limiting the growth and segregation of He bubbles. This mitigates grain-boundary embrittlement and irradiation-induced hardening, and may also contribute to improved ductility at room temperature.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to Re-free NbMoTaW, the Re-containing NbMoTaWRe will exhibit smaller, more uniform He bubbles, reduced irradiation hardening, and less pronounced grain-boundary embrittlement. These changes should improve room-temperature ductility under the specified irradiation conditions.
generation.baseline: Re-free Nb25Mo25Ta25W25 films tested under identical as-deposited and He irradiation conditions.
generation.boundary: This observed improvement is limited to magnetron-sputtered columnar nanocrystalline films on Si(111) irradiated at room temperature with the given He ion energy and dose; extrapolation to bulk materials or different processing/irradiation conditions remains unestablished.
generation.uncertainty: It remains uncertain whether the improved defect-sink properties will translate into significant improvements in high-temperature mechanical performance or in other irradiation environments beyond the specified conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of films—Re-free NbMoTaW and Re-containing NbMoTaWRe—using identical magnetron sputtering conditions on Si(111). Subject both to 120 keV He2+ irradiation (fluence: 1×10^16 ions/cm^2, dose rate: 1×10^13 ions/cm^2/s for 1000 s). Characterize He bubble size and distribution via cross-sectional TEM using FFT/ IFFT analysis, assess grain-boundary characteristics, and compare mechanical properties via nanoindentation and in situ micropillar compression.
measurements: He bubble size and distribution by TEM
Grain-boundary structure (presence of amorphous regions and segregation) via TEM/FFT-IFFT
Irradiation-induced hardening and embrittlement via nanoindentation load-displacement curves and micropillar compression tests
Damage profile estimation using SRIM simulations
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Re-containing NbMoTaWRe films do not show a statistically significant reduction in He bubble size, more uniform bubble distribution, and improvement in mechanical properties (i.e., lower irradiation hardening and reduced embrittlement) relative to the Re-free NbMoTaW films, then the hypothesis is falsified.
